Therefore, authorities have issued a yellow storm surge warning and advised preparations for wind protection.'

Okinawa Island section: 'Affected by Typhoon Khanun, the wind in Naha began to strengthen on August 8. According to local airport meteorological data, strong southeast winds persisted starting the morning of August 9, later shifting to south winds later in the morning, with brief periods of gale-force winds, followed by sustained strong winds throughout the day. As Typhoon Khanun moved away, the wind in Naha began to weaken on August 10, with strong winds subsiding in the morning and showers decreasing.'

Korea section: 'Typhoon Khanun passed over Jeju Island on the evening of August 10. During the passage of the eye, local winds temporarily calmed, and the sea level pressure dropped to 989 hPa. On August 11, Khanun also crossed the Korean Peninsula, becoming the first tropical cyclone to directly impact South Korea this year and the first since Typhoon Kalmaegi in 2008. As Khanun approached, the sea level pressure in Busan began to drop on August 10, decreasing from 1011 hPa in the morning to 1007 hPa in the evening. The southeast wind also began to strengthen in the evening, reaching gale force on August 11.'
